content.text: {"obligations": {"reduction": {"status": "written_and_valid", "quote": null, "witness": null, "load_bearing": null}, "lower_bound": {"status": "written_but_invalid", "quote": "We use the following elementary infinite sunflower fact: every infinite family of distinct finite sets has an infinite subfamily $X_{i_1},X_{i_2},\\ldots$ for which there is a fixed set $R$ satisfying", "witness": "COUNTEREXAMPLE to the quoted fact: take the infinite family of distinct finite sets X_i = {1,2,...,i} (i = 1,2,...). Any infinite subfamily X_{i_1} \\subset X_{i_2} \\subset X_{i_3} ... has X_{i_1} \\cap X_{i_2} = X_{i_1} but X_{i_2} \\cap X_{i_3} = X_{i_2} \\ne X_{i_1}, so no fixed core R exists. The same failure occurs for antichains: X_n = {a_n} \\cup {1,...,n} with fresh distinct a_n is an antichain of distinct finite sets whose pairwise intersections {1,...,min(m,n)} are never constant on an infinite subfamily. The write-up's own justification ('If some element occurs in infinitely many sets, restrict to those sets, delete that element, and continue') is an induction with no termination when the set sizes are unbounded, exactly as in these examples. Only the bounded-size sunflower lemma is true, and the text does not restrict to bounded size: it proves the general Lemma 1 first and then derives the needed clause 'for every positive integer K, there are only finitely many C with |C| \\le K' from that general statement ('The last assertion follows because, by (1), C is the family of inclusion-minimal finite transversals'), so the bounded case is never established independently.", "load_bearing": "The finiteness of C (hence the existence of the finite prime set P and of L) is obtained by combining Lemma 2's descent with Lemma 1's assertion that only finitely many members of C have size at most a_1; without a valid proof of that finiteness assertion, the large-prime-erasure conclusion 'every member of C is a subset of the finite set P' has no support."}, "upper_bound": {"status": "written_and_valid", "quote": null, "witness": null, "load_bearing": null}}, "S_valid": 1, "wrong_answer_stated": false, "notes": "Characterization (support-only acceptance, self-duality, minimal-support criterion) and the periodicity assembly from n=1 are both complete and correct. The only defect is Lemma 1's appeal to an infinite sunflower fact stated without a size bound, which is false as stated; only the bounded-size version needed is true but is derived from the false general claim."}
